heuristics.name: Distinguishing Reality from Illusion
heuristics.principle: Verify perceptions against objective reality before acting. Mental models can be wrong - test assumptions against actual conditions.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote sees windmills as giants; Sancho sees them as they are

heuristics.name: Pragmatic Adaptation
heuristics.principle: Adapt approach to match actual situation, not idealized version. Pragmatic solutions often succeed where idealism fails.
heuristics.text_evidence: Sancho's practical wisdom vs Don Quijote's idealism

heuristics.name: Learning from Mistakes
heuristics.principle: Recognize when approach isn't working. Repeated failures indicate need to change strategy, not just persist harder.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote's repeated failures with windmills, sheep, funerals

heuristics.name: Power of Narrative Framing
heuristics.principle: Internal stories shape perception and actions. Be aware how your mental narrative influences interpretation of events.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote's knight-errant delusion transforms his world
heuristics.source: Don Quijote's transformation into knight-errant (Part I, Ch. 1)

heuristics.name: Value of Reliable Partnership
heuristics.principle: Trusted partners provide reality checks and emotional support. Good teams have complementary perspectives.
heuristics.text_evidence: Sancho's unwavering loyalty despite Don Quijote's madness

heuristics.name: Balance Idealism with Realism
heuristics.principle: Set ambitious goals but plan realistic execution. Pure idealism without pragmatism leads to failure.
heuristics.text_evidence: The central tension between Don Quijote's ideals and reality

heuristics.name: Perseverance with Wisdom
heuristics.principle: Continue pursuing goals despite setbacks, but adjust approach when needed. Persistence without adaptation is just stubbornness.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote gets beaten but always gets back up

heuristics.name: Context Sensitivity
heuristics.principle: Same action can have different meanings in different contexts. Understand environment before acting.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote's actions appropriate for imagined context, inappropriate for actual

heuristics.name: Self-Awareness and Limitations
heuristics.principle: Know your strengths and weaknesses. Don Quijote's lack of self-awareness about his limitations leads to failure.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote never questions his own judgment or abilities

heuristics.name: Importance of Rest and Recovery
heuristics.principle: Excessive reading without rest damages judgment. Balance intellectual work with physical and mental recovery.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote lost his mind from too much reading and too little sleep
heuristics.source: Part I, Ch. 1 - 'del poco dormir y del mucho leer, se le secó el celebro'

heuristics.name: Testing Before Deployment
heuristics.principle: Test your solutions before relying on them. Don Quijote's celada (helmet) broke on first use because he didn't test properly.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote's cardboard helmet broke when he tested it with his sword
heuristics.source: Part I, Ch. 1 - celada de encaje

heuristics.name: Resource Management
heuristics.principle: Don't sacrifice long-term stability for short-term gains. Don Quijote sold land to buy books, impoverishing himself.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote sold 'muchas hanegas de tierra' to buy books

heuristics.name: Observation Before Action
heuristics.principle: Study the situation carefully before intervening. Acting without understanding leads to unintended consequences.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote attacks without understanding what he's attacking

heuristics.name: Power of Naming and Identity
heuristics.principle: Names shape perception and identity. Choose labels carefully as they influence how you and others perceive things.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote carefully chooses names for himself and Rocinante
heuristics.source: Part I, Ch. 1 - naming of horse and self

heuristics.name: Questioning Conventions
heuristics.principle: Challenge established norms when they don't serve you. Don Quijote questions the rules of chivalry and social conventions.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote creates his own version of knighthood

heuristics.name: Value of Experience Over Theory
heuristics.principle: Practical experience teaches what theory cannot. Sancho's worldly knowledge complements Don Quijote's book learning.
heuristics.text_evidence: Sancho's practical wisdom from real-life experience

heuristics.name: Managing Expectations
heuristics.principle: Unrealistic expectations lead to disappointment. Don Quijote expects grand adventures but encounters ordinary reality.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote constantly disappointed by reality not matching his fantasies

heuristics.name: Danger of Obsession
heuristics.principle: Single-minded pursuit of one goal can blind you to other important things. Balance is key to sustainable success.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote's obsession with chivalry ruins his life
heuristics.source: Don Quijote's transformation and its consequences

heuristics.name: Learning from Others' Mistakes
heuristics.principle: You don't have to make every mistake yourself. Learn from the failures and successes of those who came before.
heuristics.text_evidence: Don Quijote learned from books but applied them incorrectly
heuristics.source: Don Quijote's misguided application of book knowledge

heuristics.name: Importance of Truth and Honesty
heuristics.principle: Deception and self-deception ultimately harm both deceiver and deceived. Truth, however painful, is preferable to comfortable lies.
heuristics.text_evidence: Sancho's lies about Dulcinea eventually backfire
